en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever I<sup>asws</sup> narrated with anything to you all, so you should be asking me<sup>asws</sup> (where it is) from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said in one of his<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the, ‘It was said’, and ‘he said’, and the spoiling of the wealth, and the frequent questioning’. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Where is this from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying
[4:114] There is no good in most of their secret counsels except (in his) who enjoins charity or goodness or reconciliation between people.
And Said [4:5] And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has made for you a (means of) support.
And Said [5:101] O you who believe! Do not put questions about things which if declared to you may trouble you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn “isa from Yunus from Hammad from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “There is no case for which there is not a law in the book or the Sunnah, the noble tradition of the holy Prophet (s.a.)”
